messages:
matt: FYI scheduling a planned maintenance window for us-east2 GPU fleet this Friday 02:00-05:00 UTC. goal is: roll BMC firmware on 2 racks, NIC microcode update on 3 racks, and one kernel livepatch. will do rolling cordon/drain + staggered reboots to keep tail latency stable.
sarah: +1. what's the planned batch size? how many tenants will be moved at once?
matt: plan: cohorts of 6 nodes (roughly 48 GPUs) per 20m slot, sequential across racks. we keep one canary rack for 2 full cycles. backfill policy = soft backfill with burst capacity from reserve pool for 30m after each cohort.
kevin: reserve pool is ~200 GPUs in us-east today. cost estimate for burst backfill ~ $1.2k if we use full reserve for the window. can we reduce burst length to 15m to save cost?
matt: we can try 15m on non-critical racks, but keep 30m for customer-critical pools (tenant-tag: enterprise-prod).
lia: oncall check: I'll be on pager for the window and can escalate. recommend we publish a brief customer notice for tenants > 100QPS.
sarah: do we need to update routing policies so requests avoid draining nodes? (smart routing)
matt: yes — will add a transient policy: route->fallback variant for models with >1s seq latency. low-priority requests will be steered to cheaper variants. I'll post policy snippet.
kevin: can you paste drain command and safety checks? want to add to runbook.
matt: drain command we'll use: ```kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120``` followed by healthcheck script: ```/opt/realtime/ops/healthcheck.sh NODE```
ops-runbook-bot: Reminder: include KV cache warmup step post-evac: `cache-warm --pool $POOL --duration 10m` or customers will see initial latency bumps.
matt: good call. we'll run cache-warm for 10m after each cohort completes. also set perf monitor alert thresholds lower for 45m after each cohort.
sarah: what about model checkpoint restore times? some large L2 models take 90s to cold load and warmup.
matt: for models with >60s cold start we'll pre-warm on canary nodes. also enable prefix cache snapshot restore on backfill nodes.
kevin: NIC microcode step has known risk of a temporary link flap (1-2 min). will need egress QoS fallback for the rack for that 5m window. net team ok?
lia: net team signed off in doc but asked for a 15m buffer between rack updates. we'll keep 20m.
infra-bot: Deploy plan created: https://redwood.ops/runbooks/1749990000. Checklist items: pre-checks, canary, cohort schedule, rollback steps.
matt: rollback plan: if latency spike > 2x baseline for 10m or error rate > 1% rung immediate rollback: reprovision previous image + BGP re-advertise. rollback target < 30m.
sarah: who will own rollback?
matt: kevin owns rollback execution, lia owns customer comms + incident page. I'll do live orchestration.
kevin: noted. will prep playbook and a quick smoke test: `curl -sS http://canary:8080/health | jq .`
lia: customer comm draft: short blurb + expected window + tenants impacted + contact link. I'll post to #announcements 12h before.
ops-runbook-bot: Post-operation tasks: collect 30m rolling perf histograms, token-level cost delta, and generate a short incident-free summary.
sarah: one more ask: run a dry-run on Wednesday in staging with the same cohort size and warmup steps. can we do that?
matt: yes, scheduled dry-run Wed 03:00 UTC. please treat it as real — same scripts and backfill.
kevin: ok prepping reserve pool scaling script. will also add a temporary budget tag so finance can track the spend.
matt: final note: if any unexpected NIC flap leads to cross-rack congestion, we'll pause and extend window by 2h max. otherwise proceed as scheduled. thanks all :thumbsup:
lia: thumbs up. will prepare comms and oncall rota.
kevin: prepping playbook and cost tags.
sarah: I'll coordinate dry-run and verify model warmups.
infra-bot: Reminder: set SLO freeze flag at 30m before window.
matt: done. see you Friday.
